title: Break It 'Til You Make It: Building the Self-Improving Stack for AI Agents - Aparna Dhinakaran
talk_summary: Arize founder Aparna Dhinakaran lays out a layered agent-evaluation stack: tool-call correctness (right tool + right arguments), trajectory/order correctness across a trace, and multi-turn session evals that check context carry-over. Her key non-obvious point is a second improvement loop on the eval prompts themselves, since a mislabeled eval corrupts the signal you use to fix the agent.

takeaways.technique: Split tool-call eval into tool-selection vs argument-correctness
takeaways.what_they_do: Score each tool call on two independent axes: did the agent pick the right tool, and did it pass the right arguments given conversation context. They found failures where the tool was right but arguments were wrong, which a single pass/fail score would hide.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it says the function call is correct but I also have eval on did it actually pass all the right arguments

takeaways.what_they_do: Evaluate the whole trace, not just individual calls: did the agent call tools in the correct order and converge on a stable step count, or veer off and burn extra tokens re-doing steps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: is it calling tool calls in the right order ... or does it sometimes veer off and call it in a different order and therefore require me to a have to spend a lot of tokens

takeaways.technique: Multi-turn session eval for context carry-over
takeaways.what_they_do: Across a multi-turn conversation, check whether the agent uses context from turn n-1 to answer turn n, and whether it repeats questions or loses earlier context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: does it keep track of context from the previous kind of n minus one turns in order to be able to answer the nth

takeaways.technique: Second loop: improve the eval prompts, not just the agent
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat eval prompts as a living artifact with their own iteration loop and golden dataset, because a mislabeled eval wrongly flags good agent output as bad and corrupts the improvement signal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it could have been the eval that you know miscorrectly labeled it as wrong ... start to identify where the eval might need some improvements

takeaways.technique: High-level path/bottleneck dashboard before drilling into traces
takeaways.what_they_do: Start from an aggregate view across all agent paths to see which sub-path (e.g. 'search') is failing ~50/50, then drill into only those failing traces rather than reading individual traces blindly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's about half and half of times we're getting it correct as we're getting it incorrect, which is not that great
takeaways.numbers: ~50% correctness on the search path cited as the weak spot
